# Setup

This document details how to create a local copy of this pub's codebase, setup your compute environment, and reproduce the pub itself. This will enable you to experiment with the analysis in the pub and, optionally, contribute revisions to it.

## Obtain local copy

The codebase is hosted on GitHub and can be found [here](https://github.com/{{< var pub.org >}}/{{< var pub.repo >}}).

To obtain a local copy of this repo, you can either *clone* it directly or fork it to your own GitHub account, then clone your fork. If you aren't sure what's best, our suggestion is to clone directly unless you both (1) want to propose a revision for the publication and (2) are not an employee of Arcadia Science.

To clone:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/{{< var pub.org >}}/{{< var pub.repo >}}.git
```

## Installation

This repository is a [Calkit](https://docs.calkit.org) project: [`calkit.yaml`](https://github.com/{{< var pub.org >}}/{{< var pub.repo >}}/blob/main/calkit.yaml) defines the computational environment and the pipeline that produces the pub. Install [Calkit](https://docs.calkit.org/installation/), e.g., with `curl -LsSf install.calkit.org | sh` on macOS or Linux. The first time it runs, it offers to install Conda if it's missing, then creates the environment, including Quarto, from `env.yml` and the exact versions recorded in `.calkit/env-locks/`, so there's nothing else to install.

If you plan to submit a pull request, also install the [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/) hooks:

```bash
calkit xenv -n main -- pre-commit install
```

# What's next?

With a copy of the code on your local machine, you can now reproduce or modify a local copy of the publication however you see fit. Read on to get started.

## Reproduce

The best way to ensure you've correctly set up your code and compute environment is to reproduce this work:

```bash
calkit run
```

This creates the environment, then runs each pipeline stage that's out of date with its code, data, or environment, and skips the rest. On a fresh copy, everything is already up to date. To see what would run and why, use `calkit status`, and to re-execute the notebook anyway, use `calkit run notebook --force`.

The model checkpoints are committed and their training stage is frozen, since training takes a GPU and isn't bit-reproducible. See the [README](https://github.com/{{< var pub.org >}}/{{< var pub.repo >}}#reproduce) to retrain them.

To preview the site, use

```bash
make preview
```

This will open a local instance of the publication in your default browser.

## Modify

To modify or extend any analyses, open up `index.ipynb` with Jupyter (`calkit xenv -n main -- jupyter lab`) or your favorite IDE, using the environment in `.conda-envs/main`. To preview changes as you modify the notebook, run `make preview` again and leave the command running. As you make changes to the notebook, the preview site will automatically reload. When you're done, run `calkit run` so the published outputs come from a clean, top-to-bottom execution.

## Publish

If you've improved the publication, consider contributing so we can update the hosted publication with your edits (big or small!). To get started, see our [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.qmd).
